text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — I pushed a terse PRD for an Optimize Toolkit playbook (batching / prefix caching / quant recommendations) into the drive. Need a fast pass before product planning tomorrow. Main goal: provide SE-friendly, low-risk recommendations + concrete acceptance criteria so we can start advising customers without engineering changes by default.

Liam: link please, want to skim now if I can.

Maya: https://redwood.internal/drive/optimize-playbook-draft (placeholder). Sections: customer signals, auto suggestions, manual override UX, perf SLOs, rollout plan, QA checklist.

Sophie: add a section on canary/pinning interactions. Dedicated customers will insist on predictable latency with quantized variants.

Raj: also add a hard QA checklist for quant (int8/int4). We need per-prompt eval delta thresholds and an explicit opt-out.

Maya: current acceptance criteria draft in doc: 1) p50 latency improvement >= 15% on small-chat workloads when batching on; 2) token cost reduction >= 12% for medium-seq with prefix caching; 3) no >3% drop in primary metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine/intent accuracy) on customer validation set — otherwise: do not recommend quant.

Liam: prefer customer-facing metrics: embeddings -> cosine, chat -> intent classifier delta or human-rated regression.

Sophie: rollout proposal: suggestions behind feature flag for Hosted, opt-in toggle in Dedicated console. Include dry-run telemetry mode to record "what would have been recommended."

Maya: dry-run included. Also automatic rollback triggers: e.g., if latency p95 or user-facing error rate changes beyond thresholds within 4h.

Raj: we should be concrete: trigger if p95 latency increases >20% OR error rate increases >0.5% absolute over baseline for 4h.

Liam: batching edge cases to document: short-context chat (seq <64) where queueing may hurt latency; low-concurrency interactive apps; request affinity alongside KV cache.

Sophie: acceptance checks idea: interactive widgets -> max batch delay 10ms or don't batch; background/async jobs -> allow up to 200ms batch delay for throughput gains.

Maya: UX: show "Suggested optimization" in Console with expected gains, confidence score, and source eval set.

Liam: add risk level: low/medium/high. High = couldn't validate on customer data and needs SE review.

Raj: quant needs model-support matrix. Some models break on int4. PRD should include curated safe-list and a CI job that runs quantized evals across representative suites.

Sophie: I can draft the eval suites: chat: ~50 prompts across conversational templates + simulated edits; embeddings: ~10k pairs for cosine delta; reranker: MRR tests. Thresholds: cosine drop <0.02, MRR drop <1.5%.

Liam: runtime notes: need per-model, per-queue flags to toggle quant+batching; fallback to CPU decode if GPU kernel fails; per-request header to mark dry-run vs active.

Maya: rollout acceptance: Hosted feature-flag for 5% of new accounts for 2 weeks, monitor; expand to 25% then 100% if safe.

Raj: require a customer opt-out API + SE manual disable with audit log.

Sophie: edge case: stateful chat with long KV caches — caching suggestions should include TTL guidance and a cache-key schema to avoid leakage. Add an acceptance test: no cross-session leakage in 1k simulated chats.

eng-ci-bot: build report: "optimize-playbook-evals" pipeline finished: 12/15 suites passed; failing on int4 small-seq chat regression.

Maya: that's the exact failure we feared. Mark int4 as "experimental" and opt-in for customers until regression resolved.

Liam: product wants docs + console UI + telemetry + 2-week pilot with >=3 customers (Hosted, Dedicated, Enterprise) and clear rollback playbook. Eng wants runtime flag + CI gates.

Maya: agreed. Prioritized backlog in doc: 1) expand eval harness, 2) runtime flags + telemetry, 3) Console UI + messaging, 4) beta pilot ops docs, 5) public docs and examples.

Sophie: can we bundle conservative default configs for common archetypes (chat SaaS, embeddings indexer, reranker) so SEs can copy-paste?

Maya: yes — adding a config appendix with conservative defaults and a short explanation of tradeoffs.

Raj: one more: include a short-playbook for SEs that lists steps to run a dry-run, interpret metrics, and escalate to engineering if regressions occur.

Maya: will add. Also will capture acceptance criteria for canary/pinning interactions and a checklist for Dedicated rollouts.

Liam: nit: ensure the PRD calls out telemetry retention windows and the fields we need (per-request batch size, batch delay, cache hit rate, quant variant, model version).

Maya: done in doc.

Sophie: I'll draft the eval suite and thresholds by EOD. Raj, can you define the CI job spec for quantized evals?

Raj: on it. I'll also add gating rules to block auto-recommendation if model not in safe-list.

Maya: thanks all. Plan for tomorrow: 30m quick review in product planning, then finalize PRD for stakeholder signatures. If anyone has strong objections to any acceptance numbers, reply here now.

Liam: small ask — include a short examples section for SEs that shows a console screenshot + curl to opt-out. Helpful for planning.

Maya: adding examples and a sample JSON policy for opt-out.

eng-ci-bot: note: pipeline artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/optimize-playbook/artifacts/1768001234/

Raj: ok to mark this thread as the canonical quick-discussion for the PRD. I'll file a follow-up RFC for the runtime changes after EOD.

Maya: sounds good. Thanks everyone, will update the doc with the changes and tag the PRD in tomorrow's agenda.
